extracted.intended_audience: ABA members and other stakeholders submitting public comments on the Department of Education's PSLF proposed rule
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting concise, effective public comments on the Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) proposed rule, emphasizing personal/professional impact, clear asks, and submission via Regulations.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments should stay respectful and focused on practical, legal, or professional consequences; not partisan opinions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep language respectful and avoid partisan political statements. Focus comments on concrete practical, legal, or professional consequences of the proposed rule rather than ideological rhetoric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity and personalization
rubrics_metrics.description: A well-written, specific comment will carry far more weight than a form letter. Your story and professional insight help show real-world consequences the proposed rule might have.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid form letters or boilerplate language. Use a personal anecdote or professional example to illustrate how the rule affects you or your organization and to demonstrate real-world impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure and length
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be concise — ABA suggests 2–4 paragraphs (and notes a one-paragraph minimum). Short, focused comments are preferred over long, unfocused submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citations not required
rubrics_metrics.description: You do not need legal citations to be effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not feel obligated to include legal citations; the strength of the comment can come from clear, specific real-world effects and professional perspective rather than legal argumentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification / credentials
rubrics_metrics.description: My name is [Your Name], and I am a [Your Role] working in [Location/Community].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin by stating your name, role, and community or organization to establish credibility and the basis for your perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific connection to the regulatory program
rubrics_metrics.description: I rely on the Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) program to [explain how you benefit or how your organization uses PSLF].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state how you or your organization rely on or interact with PSLF so reviewers understand the direct relevance of your comment to the rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concrete impact statement
rubrics_metrics.description: If the proposed rule is implemented, it would jeopardize [describe the risk or impact].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe specific harms or risks that would occur if the rule is adopted (e.g., loss of staff, inability to serve clients). Use concrete language and, when possible, quantifiable or specific examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vulnerable population / public benefit framing
rubrics_metrics.description: PSLF has been critical for our ability to [recruit attorneys in rural areas/provide legal services/serve vulnerable clients].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame your comment to show how changes would affect vulnerable populations or public services (e.g., legal services for low-income clients, rural recruitment), emphasizing broader societal impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear ask
rubrics_metrics.description: I urge the Department to protect this vital program by revising or withdrawing the proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conclude with an explicit requested outcome (e.g., revise, withdraw, or modify the rule). A clear, specific ask helps reviewers and decisionmakers understand what action you want.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method / procedural note
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit your comment via Regulations.gov (follow the agency's posted docket and submission procedures). The ABA provides campaign-specific guidance and resources for members.
